newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediobanca, San Paolo rise on mergers talk.
newsitem.headline: Mediobanca, San Paolo rise on mergers talk.

text.p: Shares in Italian banks Mediobanca and San Paolo were firmer on the Milan stock exchange on press reports of imminent mergers in the banking sector, traders said.
At 0940 GMT, merchant bank Mediobanca was 2.32 percent higher at 10,400 lire while Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino was 1.81 percent up at 11,670.

Daily La Repubblica said in its Monday economic supplement that a plan for the incorporation of Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) into Mediobanca could be ready in coming weeks. It also said a decision was likely soon on a merger between IMI bank and San Paolo.
BCI, which said it had no comment to make on the rumours, was up 1.21 percent at 3,500. IMI was 0.34 percent off at 14,950.
"The market is reacting to the press talk but with a certain amount of caution and volumes are not high," one dealer said.
There was no comment available from the other banks.
